published_prior_art.cite: JochmansWeidner2019 supplies incidence/gauge algebra, but not an anticipation-compatible DiD fiber.
Dawid2001 defines variation independence; the bridge equivalence is a graph-specialized application.
ChenKyngLiuPengProbstGutenbergSachdeva2022 covers generic flow machinery, not coupled-anticipation endpoint certification.
Torgovitsky2019 proves subdistribution extensions in a distinct model and does not supply this announced-policy panel completion.
Fenaroli2026 gives cohortwise sharp bounds with never-treated comparisons; it explicitly leaves anticipating not-yet-treated comparison designs for future work.
Generic min-cost transshipment duality is established, but no located DiD result derives its node demand from a joint anticipation fiber.
FangLiebl2026 is asymptotic event-study inference and Fenaroli2026 uses Bayesian bootstrap rather than finite-sample outer coverage of this coupled region.
CallawaySantAnna2021 supplies the clean-anchor two-by-two reduction; the remaining calculations are diagnostics.

soundness_flags.label: Symbols Y_t^(r), G, D_t; announced-consistency; Theorems 4–6
soundness_flags.one_line: r is simultaneously used as the scheduled implementation date and as the index of an announced-decision intervention, but no decision/announcement process or implementation lag is defined, so Y_t^(r) does not uniquely specify the policy regime whose preimplementation effect is being bounded.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1 and Theorems 4–6
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Causal sharpness, transshipment endpoints, and coverage are conditional on proving the full-law completion property.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Theorems 4–6 are claims conditional on an exhaustive announced-policy completion theorem, once the announcement/implementation regime is explicitly defined.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The staggered extension uses a nonempty never-treated comparison group; it states that not-yet-treated comparisons would require accounting for their anticipation effects and names that extension as future work.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 4–5.3, lines 94–110 and 128–135; multiple-time extension lines 645–654
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper distinguishes an intervention on a policy decision/plan from implementation and represents their deterministic, lagged relationship explicitly.
PIES obtains sharpness through extension of admissible subdistributions to observationally equivalent full distributions under explicit extendibility conditions.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv corroboration; cited Journal of Econometrics version was inaccessible at DOI
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The corroborating version states limited anticipation and identifies group-time effects with either never-treated or not-yet-treated comparison groups under the corresponding assumptions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Introduce an explicit announcement/decision path P, an announcement date or known lag to implementation, and potential outcomes indexed by that path; then redefine consistency, anticipation distortion, and the ATT for the chosen decision-versus-implementation intervention.

Prove the completion construction as a theorem after the regime repair, beginning with the rational three-cohort completion and then giving the conditional-kernel construction that preserves the observed panel law.

Add a concise corollary locating Fenaroli’s never-treated design as the no-reused-comparison special case and state the strict graph condition under which the proposed joint region collapses to independently computed bounds.

recommended_next_step: Revise the causal regime indexing to separate announcement decisions from implementation, then retain the accepted conditional completion scope and advance the repaired kernel to Stage 0.
